# Rubik's Graph Lab v0.1.0

The first research release of Rubik's Graph Lab brings the browser app, COVE-3 practical solver, exact-search visualizations, and the accompanying research paper together in one reproducible snapshot.

## Highlights

- Solve valid 3×3 states with COVE-3, the project's compact, work-bounded two-phase configuration. The solver runs in a cancellable browser worker and only presents a solution after cubie and sticker replay checks.
- Explore BFS, bidirectional BFS, and A* on manageable 2×2 and 3×3 scrambles, with graph and depth visualizations. Completed exact searches retain their shortest-path guarantees.
- Enter a scramble or use two cube photos, correct the recognized sticker map, validate the state, and replay the resulting moves on a 3D cube.
- Read the [seven-page research paper](https://github.com/nahin333/rubikscube/blob/main/research/paper.pdf) and inspect [all 200 paired measurements](https://github.com/nahin333/rubikscube/blob/main/research/results/solver-comparison.json).

## Recorded comparison

On 200 shared, seeded 20–40-turn scrambles, COVE-3 had a median warm solve time of **5.965 ms**, versus **34.047 ms** for cubejs 1.3.2. COVE-3 returned longer solutions on average: **22.77** versus **21.71** moves. Both configurations passed sticker replay on all 200 evaluated cases. These are local Node measurements on one machine, not a universal speed or optimality claim.

## Scope and access

Use the app at https://nahin333.github.io/rubikscube/ — no server installation is required. This release supports the documented 2×2 and 3×3 models; it does **not** implement arbitrary-size cube reduction. COVE-3 can exhaust its search budget on a valid cube and does not guarantee shortest solutions. The photo workflow requires user alignment and correction; autonomous vision accuracy was not evaluated.

The attached `paper.pdf` is the same paper committed under `research/paper.pdf`. Its CVPR author-kit styling is a formatting choice, not a conference submission or acceptance claim.
